newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eureko worried over EU terms on GAN sale.
newsitem.headline: Eureko worried over EU terms on GAN sale.

text.p: The head of the Eureko group which is bidding for troubled French insurer GAN said on Wednesday it was concerned by a French government promise to the European Commission that half of GAN's foreign operations would be sold off.

Jeff Medlock, head of the Eureko group of six European insurers, told newspaper Les Echos the forced sale of activities, especially within as short a time as the stipulated 12 months, was a concern for bidders interested in GAN's international network.

"We find the demand for the sale of foreign activities strange, especially in a period as short as 12 months. This could be troublesome for candidates interested in the international network," he said.
Eureko was keen on the 'bancassurance' concept -- a mix of banking and insurance activities -- and wants to keep a stake of between 25-30 percent in the CIC bank network owned by GAN, he said.
The GAN management shared this view, Medlock said, adding he did not think this posed a problem for the majority shareholder.
"We have no presence in banking in France and we are open to collaboration," he said.

The European Commission recently approved a 20-billion-franc state rescue package for GAN in return for a government pledge to launch the privatisation of GAN and CIC by mid-1998 at the latest and to sell half of GAN's activities outside France.

Eureko is an alliance of six European financial service companies, comprising Dutch Achmea, Portuguese BCP/Atlantico, Britain's Friends Provident, Gothaer of Germany, Denmark's Topdanmark and Wasa of Sweden.

Medlock has said Eureko members would pay with both loans and new shares if it succeeds in acquiring state-controlled insurer GAN. Debt would be required as bridging capital ahead of the intended listing of Eureko about two years time.
Eureko aims to list 49-50 percent of the total group in Amsterdam, Paris and, probably, London. It would jump from the seventh to the third biggest insurance group in Europe.
It was looking for a 100 percent stake in GAN and it would not be interested in sharing ownership of the French insurer.
